hypotheses.justification: The statement is still true without quasi-compactness, but the proof has to change. In Mathlib, `Scheme.Hom.ker f` is defined as `ofIdeals (fun U ↦ RingHom.ker (f.app U).hom)`, the largest ideal sheaf contained in the componentwise kernels. QuasiCompact is only used to identify `f.ker.ideal U` with `RingHom.ker (f.app U)` (`Hom.ker_apply`) and to get `Hom.support_ker`. For each j, `(f j).ker = vanishingIdeal (closure (range (f j)))` holds for any morphism from a reduced scheme. The ≤ direction does not need QC: `Hom.range_subset_ker_support` has no QC hypothesis, and closedness of the support gives `closure (range f) ≤ f.ker.support`. So `f.ker ≤ vanishingIdeal f.ker.support ≤ vanishingIdeal (closure (range f))`, using `vanishingIdeal_support` (the vanishing ideal of the support is the radical, which is ≥ I) together with antitonicity of `vanishingIdeal`. For ≥, use `le_ofIdeals_iff` to reduce to showing that every `s` in `(vanishingIdeal (closure (range f))).ideal U` satisfies `f.app U s = 0`. Such an `s` lies in every prime `p` of Γ(Y,U) whose point lies in the closure of the range. For each `x ∈ f⁻¹U`, `f x` lies in the range, so `x ∉ basicOpen (f.app U s) = f⁻¹(basicOpen s)`. Hence `basicOpen (f.app U s) = ⊥`, and since X is reduced, `f.app U s = 0`. Taking the infimum over j then goes through exactly as in the existing proof, via `vanishingIdeal_iSup`. IsReduced is genuinely needed: for the identity on a non-reduced scheme the kernel is ⊥ but the vanishing ideal of ⊤ is the nilradical.
